note: Built-in convex guidance profiles, one per mission type and corridor behaviour. Each entry is a bounded override of configs/controllers/convex_guidance.yaml validated by convex_parameters.validate_settings. Tracking gains kp/kd/ki are never changed: the 1.0/1.2/0.3 horizontal set is the one the hover-loop damping analysis (zeta 0.37) and the Isaac sweeps chose, and kd 1.6 wobbled in terminal descent. tilt_rate_authority_fraction stays at 0.4 in every profile: planning the thrust-rate bound's ~30 deg/s slew saturated every vane offline (2026-09-25). Tracking max tilt always keeps >= 7 deg of margin over the planned tilt for feedback. Route-following profiles (2026-09-28) add secondary objective terms (path, smoothness, time and tilt weights, priced in seconds of hover cost) and the fly-through arrival cone. The evidence is the offline closed-loop matrix in docs/convex_multi_objective_2026-09-28.md (momentum-vane plant + the mission sequencer), not yet Isaac runs.

profiles.name: Hop - gentle low tilt
profiles.summary: First hops and short pad-to-pad transfers: slow, near-vertical thrust, generous margins.
profiles.rationale: 8 deg planned tilt and 2 m/s keep lateral acceleration under ~1.4 m/s^2, leaving most of the vane authority for disturbance rejection. The corridor penalty is raised 2.5x so a short arc is followed closely without giving up the soft emergency fallback. Path weight 10 prices cross-track distance inside the corridor too (the energy optimum otherwise rides its edge); smoothness 1 keeps planned jerk low.

profiles.name: Hop - soft corridor
profiles.summary: General takeoff, transfer and landing hops. Follows the drawn arc but always gets a plan.
profiles.rationale: Repository tilt limits with a 3 m/s speed cap suited to hops under ~20 m. Corridor excess priced at 25 s of hover energy per m*s (default 10); soft mode still brakes an over-speed start at full thrust when the corridor is unreachable. Path weight 10 pulls the plan onto the drawn route inside the corridor (offline closed loop: cross-track RMS 0.31 -> 0.16 m on the slalom, 0.32 -> 0.13 m on the remote-pad approach), and gates are crossed at 50-100% of the leg speed within 20 deg of the route so tight turns stay feasible under the 10 deg/s slew bound. Smoothness 1 limits planned jerk.

profiles.name: Hop - strict corridor
profiles.summary: Hops that must stay inside the corridor (obstacles, test-range limits). Holds instead of leaving it.
profiles.rationale: Strict corridors reject any plan with slack and hold if infeasible, so the profile keeps plans comfortably feasible: 2.5 m/s, 12 deg planned tilt and a 1 m half-width. Tighter re-plan triggers (0.6 m, 0.6 m/s) restart from the measured state before the tube is exhausted. With exact gate velocities the eight-gate weaving corridor (sample 25) had no strict plan and held on the pad for its whole timeout offline; the arrival cone (50-100% of leg speed, within 20 deg of the route) flew it 11/11 at 0.14-0.16 m cross-track RMS. Path weight 10 and smoothness 1 keep the plan on the centreline and the vanes out of saturation.

profiles.name: Hop - agile wide tilt
profiles.summary: Longer, faster transfers (10-20 m). Wider tilt cone and speed, looser corridor.
profiles.rationale: 20 deg planned tilt still leaves 1.2 W * cos 20 = 1.13 W of vertical thrust inside the planning ceiling (8S, T/W 1.41, half the excess reserved). Tracking tilt 28 deg keeps 8 deg of feedback margin and the correction bound rises to 3.5 m/s^2. The tilt-rate share is unchanged (0.4): the cone widens, the slew does not. Path weight 10 cut the agile transfer's cross-track RMS 0.22 -> 0.15 m offline. Gates keep the exact leg speed: the arrival cone let the figure eight slow at every gate (+20-30% time and energy), which defeats this profile's purpose.

profiles.name: Hop - time weighted agile
profiles.summary: Long, fast transfers where arrival time matters as well as energy. Agile limits, time priced.
profiles.rationale: Agile limits (20 deg, 5 m/s) with time_weight 1.0: every second of plan costs one extra second of hover power, doubling the implicit time price energy already pays, and the planner also tries 0.8x waypoint-leg timings. Gates may slow only to 70% of the leg speed within 15 deg, so the cone keeps turns feasible without trading the speed away; path weight 5 and smoothness 1 keep the fast plan trackable.

profiles.name: Hover - precision hold strict
profiles.summary: Station keeping and slow survey points with tight capture. Strict tube between hold points.
profiles.rationale: 1.5 m/s and 10 deg planned tilt make every hold approach gentle so the 0.4 m/s capture gate is met on arrival. 0.75 m strict corridor between closely spaced hover points; re-plans every 0.4 s from a 0.5 m / 0.5 m/s error so the hold reference stays current. Fly-throughs aim inside 40% of their radius and may cross at 50-100% of the leg speed within 20 deg (a strict tube with exact gate velocities can have no plan at all). Path weight 10 and smoothness 1 cut cross-track RMS 0.16 -> 0.03 m on the compass and 0.32 -> 0.04 m on the survey box offline.

profiles.name: Hover - gust tolerant soft
profiles.summary: Holding position in wind and gusts. Reserves more thrust and tilt for feedback.
profiles.rationale: The plan withholds 60% (default 50%) of the thrust above weight for the tracking loop, and the command tilt limit rises to 26 deg with a 4 m/s^2 correction bound so a 5 m/s gust can be rejected without the plan itself tilting further. A 1.5 m soft corridor absorbs gust drift instead of forcing aggressive re-routing.

profiles.name: Hover - attitude reserve
profiles.summary: Long holds and relocations in strong wind: the plan itself tilts and slews as little as possible.
profiles.rationale: Hover-gust thrust reserve and feedback bounds, plus tilt weight 3 (one second at the 15 deg planned tilt costs 3 s of hover) and smoothness 2, so the plan leaves attitude and vane authority to the wind trim instead of spending it on its own manoeuvres. Path weight 5 keeps relocations on the drawn route. The tilt term's gust benefit is a planner-level argument: the offline plant has no wind model, so it needs Isaac confirmation.

profiles.name: Hover - endurance efficient
profiles.summary: Long holds and slow repositioning in calm air with minimum electrical energy.
profiles.rationale: Energy objective with 2 m/s and 10 deg keeps transfer legs near hover power. A wide, cheaply priced corridor (2 m, weight 5) lets the optimizer take the lowest-energy path. Two solver workers and a 0.75 s re-plan period reduce CPU load on long runs; the landing leg still freezes 0.8 s before the gate.

profiles.name: Landing - precision strict
profiles.summary: Pad-centred landings with a narrow approach cone. Strict corridor on any routed approach.
profiles.rationale: 40 deg glide slope finishes lateral motion higher than the 45 deg default (45 landed 0.29 m from centre where 55 missed by 0.68 m and 70 by 0.58 m; missions c2090264e9af, f546162f3741). The gate is raised to 0.6 m and hands over only within 0.25 m, then full descent rate only within 0.15 m of centre. 30 landing nodes resolve the narrower cone. With exact gate velocities the strict descending dogleg (sample 27) had no plan and held until timeout offline; the arrival cone (50-100%, 20 deg) landed it 6/6 on the pad at 0.12 m/s with 0.10-0.14 m cross-track RMS. Path weight 10 and smoothness 1 hold the routed approach on the centreline.

profiles.name: Landing - routed approach tracking
profiles.summary: Landings after a drawn approach (circuits, go-arounds, spirals). Follows the route hard but always gets a plan.
profiles.rationale: Soft 1.5 m corridor priced at 25 s per m*s plus path weight 15, so the approach stays on the drawn curve without the strict tube's hold-if-infeasible failure mode. Gates may cross at 50-100% of the leg speed within 25 deg, which keeps turning descents feasible under the 10 deg/s slew bound; smoothness 1 limits planned jerk. The glide slope and its 4 s narrowing match land-precision.

profiles.name: Landing - soft touchdown
profiles.summary: Gentle final descent for sensitive payloads or noisy sensors. Lower planned sink acceleration.
profiles.rationale: descent_brake_ratio 0.8 raises the thrust floor so planned downward acceleration never exceeds 80% of the braking acceleration (a 6S plan that out-fell its braking hit at 2.1 m/s, mission 201f2c58bb9e). The gate is raised to 0.8 m for a longer settled vertical segment. Pair it with a Landing step at 0.10-0.12 m/s: that step sets the terminal descent clamp (1.2x touchdown speed).

profiles.name: Landing - crosswind soft
profiles.summary: Landings in steady crosswind and gusts, or after an attitude upset. More feedback authority.
profiles.rationale: A 70 deg cone let a crosswind approach brake 2.2 m/s sideways at 1.1 m and miss by 0.58 m (mission f546162f3741), so the cone is 40 deg with 4 s of narrowing. Tracking tilt 26 deg, 4 m/s^2 correction and a 60% thrust reserve hold the wind trim; terminal full-rate centring widens to 0.3 m so a gust does not stall the descent off centre (0289417f5d60 stalled until timeout).

profiles.name: Landing - high altitude fast
profiles.summary: Descents from 25-40 m or fast-falling starts. Higher speed cone and finer long-leg resolution.
profiles.rationale: 6 m/s lets a 30 m descent finish in reasonable time; an over-speed start keeps its speed and brakes back under the cap rather than ratcheting it (0289417f5d60). 32 landing nodes, 50 nodes per leg and a 0.6 s solve budget with a 0.6 s re-plan period resolve the longer powered descent without re-solving faster than the solver can finish.

profiles.name: Landing - delta-v objective
profiles.summary: Research comparison: minimise propulsive delta-v (the paper's fuel analog) instead of energy.
profiles.rationale: Identical constraints to the repository defaults; only the cost changes from electrical Wh to the integral of |T|/m, so energy and delta-v trajectories can be compared on the same mission and seed.
